checks.reason: This is an English-only rendering of the critical note I approved earlier (s0168-literal), and it keeps every substantive element. It keeps the word-by-word rendering of the extant 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝 ('I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you'), and 'probably corrupt' still reflects the commentary's 疑. It attributes that judgment to the Jinshu Jiaozhu (晉書斠注). It gives the Tongjian reading 恨恨不欲殺汝 as 'with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you', consistent with the gloss 恨恨相戀之情. It gives Yulan 744's citation of the 前燕錄, translated 'Records of Former Yan', as 誓不殺汝, 'I swear not to kill you'. These all match the supplied 斠注 quote. The only change is dropping the Han-character forms, which stay in the separately displayed Chinese source. No Chinese is changed, nothing is silently emended, and the idiomatic field ('I should have killed you') follows the same extant text.
checks.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you [the extant wording is probably corrupt (Jinshu Jiaozhu): the Tongjian reads “with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you”; Yulan 744, quoting the Records of Former Yan, reads “I swear not to kill you”].

cautions: This is an editorial review of English wording only. It is not approval of any date, identity, chapter or publication, and it does not clear any attribution or chronology hold.
